title: Continuing the Suspension of Duty-Free De Minimis Treatment for All Countries

enrichment.summary: This executive order continues the suspension of the duty-free de minimis exemption for imported goods from all countries, meaning U.S. Customs and Border Protection will collect duties on most shipments, including those sent through the international postal network. The order updates previous rules and duty rates to help address national emergencies related to trade and illicit imports, ensuring customs duties are properly collected to protect U.S. interests.
potential_concerns: The continued suspension of duty-free de minimis treatment and collection of additional duties may increase costs for small business owners and manufacturers who rely on imported materials, potentially raising prices for consumers and reducing competitiveness.
Increased tariffs and duties on low-value international postal shipments could disproportionately burden low-income individuals and families who depend on affordable imported goods.
Retail workers may experience negative impacts if higher import costs lead to reduced sales or store closures due to decreased consumer purchasing power.

The expanded duty collection on international postal shipments might lead to logistical and administrative challenges for carriers, slowing delivery times and increasing costs, indirectly affecting consumers.
